prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1236; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a sideswipe that occurred while the insured was changing lanes. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact will go through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record. The driver involved is named on the policy, and coverage was in force at the time of loss.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. It confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene, and the responding officer's description of the lane change matches the insured's account.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the shop show damage that lines up with the described impact. Some details are visible in the images, but no independent witnesses have come forward.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who outlined neck and back strain as the injuries. The reported injury is plausible for a collision of this type.

Entry 6: Checked prior claims and medical history available to us. No earlier injury to the same body area is known, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is on record.

Entry 7: Claimant's account was given again during a follow-up call and matched the earlier statements in every key point.

Entry 8: Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. Vehicle inspection notes are consistent with a recent loss.

Entry 9: Treatment records received. The care followed a usual course for this type of strain, with physical therapy and medication.

Entry 10: Updated treatment notes show the claimant improving steadily, and the visits have tapered as symptoms eased.

Entry 11: File is progressing normally. Remaining items are the final treatment bill and the attorney's settlement demand, and no coverage questions are open.
